transcript.content: hey, i'm berry. whatever you remember from your dream, small or strange, i'd love to hear it.
The part that stuck with me was the suitcase full of letters, all addressed to me.
a whole suitcase, just for you. that must have felt heavy in a way that wasn't just the weight.
Yeah, exactly. He didn’t say anything either, just opened it so I could see them all.
the silence makes it heavier somehow. no explanation, just all those words waiting for you.
Right. And the train was so quiet too, moving through all that snow at night.
quiet everywhere. was the snow outside the only thing moving, then?
Just the snow and the train. Everything else was still. The window was all white and blue.
white and blue, cold colors. did the cold come through the window, or stay outside?
It stayed outside, but the inside wasn’t warm either. Just kind of still and dim.
like the cold had a presence, even through the glass. what happened next, after he opened the suitcase?
The train stopped, right in the middle of a snowy field. We both got off.
so it became a different world altogether. what was it like when you got off into the snow?
Deep snow, we had to wade through it. There was nothing around except this red door standing on its own in its frame.
a red door just standing there, no house, nothing else. did either of you reach for it?
He gave me the suitcase first, then nodded at the door. I opened it.
a silent hand-off. he seemed to know what was next. what was on the other side?
Warm yellow light, spilling out. That’s where it ended.
warm yellow light, after all that cold. and the man with the suitcase — was he someone you knew, or a stranger?
He was my grandfather. He died years ago.
that changes the whole thing, doesn't it? your grandfather handing you all those letters in the snow, no words needed. and you just knew it was him?
Yeah, I just knew. He looked how I remember him, sitting across from me on that train.
so you were aware all through it that he was gone, even while he sat with you like before. how did that feel, to be on a quiet train with him again?
Not scary, not sad exactly. Just strange and real at the same time. Like it made sense, somehow.
dreams can be like that — impossible and still full of sense. what did the suitcase itself look like, if you remember?
It was brown leather, old. He kept it on his knees before he opened it.
old brown leather, kept close. did he have it with him the whole time, or did it just appear when the dream got going?
He had it with him the whole time, from when I first noticed him on the train.

here's what i heard: you were on a quiet train at night, moving through snow, everything still and dim, the window all white and blue. your grandfather, who died years ago, sat across from you with an old brown leather suitcase on his knees. without a word, he opened it to show letters addressed to you. the train stopped in a snowy field, you both got off into deep snow, and there was nothing around but a red door standing on its own. he handed you the suitcase, nodded at the door, you opened it, and warm yellow light spilled out. that's where it ended. it felt strange and real, not scary or sad, like it just made sense.

did i get that right, or did i miss anything?
That’s right. You got it all.
thank you for telling me all that. would you like to see it drawn?
Yes, I would.

i can think of a few ways to draw it. one feels like a cold blue and white illustration, soft and quiet, like a breath on cold glass. another is a flat and silent graphic print, bold shapes and utter silence, each colour immutable. there's also a faded and ghostly photograph, like a memory that's almost gone, pale and wavering. and then a photograph, a window into the dream itself, faithful to every quiet and strange detail.

which of these feels closest to how you'd want it, or would you describe your own way?
A photograph, a window into the dream itself.

a photograph then. i'll start with your grandfather, just on his own.

i'm picturing him the way you remember him — older, gentle features, quiet and calm. these are my guesses, though. does anything feel different, or should i leave it to you?
He was older, yeah, gentle and calm. That fits. I don't remember his clothes clearly, so your guess is fine.

i'm sketching your grandfather and the train car and the snowy field and the red door and the suitcase now, and it'll appear on the right — just those for now, nothing else yet.

and i'll draw you too, since you're in it. how would you like to be drawn — the way you actually look, and you can tell me a little about yourself, or however i imagine you?
However you imagine me is fine.
alright, i'll imagine you as i like. everything's being sketched now, and it'll appear on the right over the next minute or two. if anything looks off once it's there, just say so.
Oh, it’s up. It looks right.
does it look the way you remember?
Yeah, it does. The train, the snow, the red door — all like I saw it.

that's good to hear. it means the sketch caught the dream right.

i'll draw the moments of the dream in order now, each one carrying on from the ones before it. they'll appear on the right as they're ready.
Okay.
good. i'll keep drawing the next moments now, one after another.
Alright, I’ll wait.

okay, take your time.

the rest of the moments are still being drawn, they'll appear on the right as they're ready.
No rush.

no rush at all. i'll keep drawing the rest in the background.

two moments are up now: him opening the suitcase with all those letters, and the train window with white and blue snow outside. do they look the way you saw them?
Yeah, both look right. The letters and the snow out the window.

good, those two are right then.

the rest of the moments are still being drawn, they'll appear on the right as they're ready.
Okay.
The train stopping in the snowy field is up now. Does it look the way you remember?
Yeah, it does. Stopped in the middle of all that snow, nothing around.
good, that one's right too. the rest are still being drawn, they'll appear on the right soon.
Sounds good.

the next moment is up: you and your grandfather wading through deep snow, heading towards the red door. once you say this one looks right, the next moments will carry on from it.

does it look the way you remember?
Yeah, that’s how it was. The snow was deep, up past our knees.

good, that one's right too.

the last two moments are still being drawn, they'll appear on the right soon.
Okay.

the moment where he hands you the suitcase is up now.

does it look the way you remember?
